definitions.explanation: Amplitude modulation radio broadcasting, which has longer range than FM but lower audio quality.

examples.japanese: AM{放送|ほうそう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聴|き}く→聴く：30010_kiku⟧。
⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧AM⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{電波|でんぱ}→電波：04070_denpa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{届|とど}く→届く：00899_todoku⟧。
examples.english: AM signals travel well at night.

examples.japanese: AM⟦ラジオ→ラジオ：01541_rajio⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{野球|やきゅう}→野球：04727_yakyuu⟧⟦{中継|ちゅうけい}→中継：11306_chuukei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聴|き}いた→聴く：30010_kiku⟧。
examples.english: I listened to the baseball broadcast on AM radio.

notes:
AM stands for amplitude modulation ({振幅|しんぷく}{変調|へんちょう}). It has longer transmission range than FM, especially at night.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- AM{放送|ほうそう}: AM broadcasting
- AM⟦{局|きょく}→局：02687_kyoku⟧: AM station
- AM⟦ラジオ→ラジオ：01541_rajio⟧: AM radio
- AM⟦{番組|ばんぐみ}→番組：01705_bangumi⟧: AM program

CULTURAL NOTE:
AM radio is popular for news, talk shows, and sports broadcasts. Many Japanese AM stations simulcast on FM (⟦ワイド→ワイド：11403_waido⟧FM) for better sound quality in urban areas.

Note: AM/PM (⟦{午前|ごぜん}→午前：00548_gozen⟧/⟦{午後|ごご}→午後：00544_gogo⟧) time notation uses the same letters but is pronounced differently.
